To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the environmental performance of a biohydrogen production system can be improved by up to 40% by implementing more efficient agricultural practices, and that the use of biohydrogen as a replacement of conventional hydrogen can reduce global warming by up to 90%.

(i) the environmental impact of biohydrogen production can be reduced significantly by improving the efficiency of the agricultural practices of the feedstock; (ii) the environmental performance of the system is improved even more if the biomass production is optimized to minimize the environmental impacts; and (iii) this type of bio-energy system can be an attractive alternative to conventional hydrogen in terms environmental impact and energy demand.
the environmental performance of hydrogen from gasification of vineyard pruning is improved by 40% if the pruning is done more efficiently.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a quantitative approach to evaluate the influence of operational efficiency in the life-cycle performance and sustainability of biohydrogen.
the quantification of the influence of agricultural practices on the life cycle of biohydrogen and the identification of the most efficient practices.
the quantification of the environmental performance of a hydrogen system from biomass gasification, with special emphasis on the role of agricultural practices.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, although biohydrogen is a very promising alternative to conventional hydrogen, the fulfilment of agricultural best practices is a key issue to enhance its environmental performance.
the use of hydrogen from biomass as a substitute for conventional hydrogen can be environmentally beneficial.
the environmental impact of biohydrogen can be improved by optimising the operational practices of the biomass feedstock production.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
bioenergy systems can be an excellent substitute for conventional energy systems in terms of global climate impact, but only if they are operated efficiently.

the environmental profile of the system is strongly affected by the efficiency with which biomass is produced, and that the environmental profile is improved significantly by fulfilling the benchmarks of operational efficiency.

, in order to achieve the best performance, it is necessary to improve the efficiency of the agricultural practices, and that the use of biohydrogen is a good choice for the future, but only if the efficiency of the production is improved.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the environmental performance of hydrogen from bioenergy can be significantly improved by optimising the agricultural production of the biomass feedstock.
a more sustainable biohydrogen production is feasible through the optimisation of the agricultural phase of bioenergy supply chains.
the life-cycle environmental performance of bioenergy systems can be enhanced through the application of operational benchmarks, which can be obtained by using data envelopment analysis.
